title: Connecting platforms to Advanced SSPM: the platforms the connect page lists and what each needs

prose.label: What the pages do not say.
prose.text: The nine per-platform pages carry no permissions table, reconnect, edit or delete section, or ingest-delay note {{gap:missing-per-platform-data}}. The application lists on other pages differ, see [[zia.sspm]].

direct-connect-list.statement: The Advanced SSPM connect page lists the API-based platforms Adobe Acrobat Sign, Airtable, Bitwarden, Databricks, Kintone, Lucid, OneLogin, OpenAI, Sentry, Smartsheet and Zendesk, and says that onboarding some API-based platforms redirects to the Add SaaS Application Tenant page in the Zscaler Admin Console.

quotes: You can connect the following API-based platforms to Advanced SSPM:
- Adobe Acrobat Sign - Airtable - Bitwarden - Databricks - Kintone - Lucid - OneLogin - OpenAI - Sentry - Smartsheet - Zendesk
For onboarding some of the API-based platforms, you are redirected to the Add SaaS Application Tenant page in the Zscaler Admin Console.

advanced-license.statement: Connecting a platform to Advanced SSPM is dependent on the license.

quotes: Connecting your platform to Advanced SSPM is dependent on your license.

connect-result.statement: After a connection is achieved, pulling and ingesting the application data might take a while depending on the tenant's size. After integration completes, a success message appears and the integration status, first connected time and last synced time are updated on the Settings page; if the connection fails, an error message appears.

quotes: After a connection is achieved, it might take a while to pull and ingest all relevant application data depending on the size of your tenant.

After integration is completed, a success message appears, and the integration status, first connected time, and last synced time are updated on the Settings page. If the connection fails, an error message appears.

platform-roles-and-credentials.statement: Each platform's page names its connecting role and credentials. Airtable needs an Airtable Admin and the Enterprise Account ID, then Grant access. Bitwarden needs an Owner and the domain suffix, client ID and client secret from the Organization info page. Databricks needs an Account Admin, the account ID and the client ID and secret of an account-level service principal with the Account Admin role. Lucid needs an Account Admin, SCIM integration enabled, a SCIM token and an API key. OneLogin needs an Account Owner or Admin and the subdomain, client ID and client secret. OpenAI needs an Organization Owner and an API key set to Read-only. Sentry needs a Manager or Owner, and shows the consent window on the first integration. Smartsheet needs a System Admin and an API access token, with a product selection if the tenant is in a non-default region. Zendesk needs an Admin, an API token and the token owner's email address.

quotes: A user with Airtable Admin privileges is required to connect Advanced SSPM to your Airtable organization.
In the Add Integration window, enter your Airtable Enterprise Account ID, and then click Add.
Click Grant access, and grant approvals if prompted.
A user with Owner privileges is required to connect Advanced SSPM to your Bitwarden organization.
In the Add Integration window, enter the Bitwarden Domain Suffix (e.g., com, eu), Client ID, and Client Secret, and then click Connect.
You can find the Client ID and Client Secret on the Organization info page of the Bitwarden Admin Console.
A user with Account Admin privileges is required to connect Advanced SSPM to your Databricks organization.
Enter your Databricks Account ID.
Create an account-level service principal.
Assign the Account Admin role to the service principal.
Enter the Client ID and Client secret.
A user with Account Admin privileges is required to connect Advanced SSPM to your Lucid organization.
Ensure SCIM integration is enabled.
Paste the token under SCIM token back in the Add Integration window.
Paste the key under API key in the Add Integration window.
A user with Account Owner or Admin privileges is required to connect Advanced SSPM to your OneLogin organization.
In the Add Integration window, enter the OneLogin subdomain (e.g., acme), Client ID, and Client Secret, and then click Connect.
A user with Organization Owner privileges is required to connect Advanced SSPM to your OpenAI organization.
When creating the API key, ensure to set the permissions to Read-only.
A user with Manager or Owner privileges is required to connect Advanced SSPM to your Sentry organization.
If you are integrating Zscaler SaaS Security with Sentry for the first time, the consent window appears, else the integration continues without displaying the consent window.
A user with System Admin privileges is required to connect Advanced SSPM to your Smartsheet organization.
In the Add Integration window, select the relevant product from the drop-down menu, if your tenant resides in one of the non-default regions.
Paste the token under API access token in the Add Integration window.
A user with Admin privileges is required to connect Advanced SSPM to your Zendesk organization.
Back in the Add Integration window, paste the newly generated API token under API token.
Enter the email address of the Zendesk admin who generated the token under API token owner email.

lucid-api-key.statement: The Lucid API key is set with the permissions Documents Readonly, Folders Readonly, Users View, Accounts Admin, Teams Admin and Licenses None, and the page recommends an expiration date at least one year away to avoid reintegrating the platform frequently.

quotes: Documents: Readonly
Folders: Readonly
Users: View
Accounts: Admin
Teams: Admin
Licenses: None
It is recommended to set the expiration date to at least one year away to avoid reintegrating the platform frequently.

missing-per-platform-data.title: What the Advanced SSPM platform pages leave out
missing-per-platform-data.detail: None of the captured Advanced SSPM pages for the nine directly connected platforms has a permissions table, or a Reconnect, Edit or Delete section, and none mentions the ingest delay or a readiness email that the 3rd-Party App Governance pages carry. The absence is from reading those pages, not a statement that the behavior does not exist.
